organizations.What they build: German maker of 'cognitive' robots: collaborative arms (MAiRA, LARA), mobile platforms (MAV, MiPA) and the humanoid 4NE1. In Oct 2026 it launched 4NE1 Gen 4 (20% lighter, built for series production) and Neuron AI, its own multimodal foundation model (vision, touch, audio, robot state, language). With TUM it opened a €17M 'RoboGym' training centre near Munich airport. June 2026: Series C of up to $1.4B led by Tether (Amazon, Nvidia, Qualcomm, Bosch, Schaeffler, EIB also in); full disbursement depends on milestones per CNBC; valuation ~$7B per Bloomberg (not confirmed by NEURA).
organizations._relationship_reason: Very well funded and building a public training-centre network (TUM RoboGym); a talk or visit is plausible, but hardware donations to a student lab are unlikely (humanoids are expensive).

organizations.What they build: Munich physical-AI company (DLR roots) making force-controlled robot arms (Diana 7, Thor series), the Agile Hand, mobile robots, production cells and humanoids with legs or wheels (Agile ONE). Owns Franka Robotics since 2023. Nov 2026: raised $500M led by SoftBank (Nvidia, Hitachi, T.Capital) at an $8.5B valuation, ~$2B raised in total.
organizations._relationship_reason: Largest-valued European robot platform startup; via its Franka subsidiary it already serves research labs, so a research/education partnership is the most realistic route.

organizations.What they build: Maker of the Franka Research 3 (FR3), a 7-joint arm with torque sensors in every joint and 1 kHz low-level control: the 'reference' arm used in many robot-learning papers. Also sells FR3 Duo, a mobile FR3 and GELLO teleoperation kits. Founded 2016, part of Agile Robots since 2023.
organizations._relationship_reason: Research-first company with a community forum and webinars; an academic discount or loan of an FR3 is the kind of deal it targets, but terms are unknown.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public community forum and webinars on franka.de (no named contact)

organizations.What they build: Danish pioneer of collaborative robot arms ('cobots', arms safe enough to work next to people), part of US group Teradyne Robotics; 100,000+ deployments, payloads up to 35 kg. Sept 2026: launched Gen 7 (new g-Series arms, CB7 controller, PolyScope X software) designed for AI. March 2026: launched the UR AI Trainer imitation-learning data system with Scale AI.
organizations._relationship_reason: Runs the UR Academy (free online training) and a large partner ecosystem; cobot loans for education are common in the industry, but no specific programme was verified.

organizations.What they build: One of the 'big four' industrial robot makers (founded 1898 in Augsburg, owned by China's Midea since 2016/17): industrial arms, AMRs and production systems; ~€3.9B sales, ~14,500 employees. In 2026 it partnered with Nvidia on 'Automation 2.0' (physical AI) and launched an AI 2D/3D vision system.
organizations._relationship_reason: Large corporate with KUKA College training; sponsorship is possible through its French subsidiary but no lab programme was verified.

organizations.What they build: Robotics division of Swiss-Swedish ABB: industrial and collaborative arms, AMRs, controllers and software, 7,000+ employees. ABB agreed in Oct 2025 to sell it to SoftBank ($5.375B); on 5 Nov 2026 China blocked the deal for the China business, and ABB and SoftBank are discussing options. Its ownership may change.
organizations._relationship_reason: Big industrial player; useful for talks and industrial-robot exposure, but the pending sale makes new partnerships uncertain.

organizations.What they build: ETH Zurich spin-off (2016) building ANYmal, a four-legged autonomous inspection robot for oil & gas, power and mining plants. Oct 2026: started deliveries of ANYmal X, certified for explosive atmospheres (ATEX/IECEx), first customers Equinor and DSM-Firmenich. Series B closed at $110M (Dec 2024); EU-Startups reported a further €127M+ raise in Sept 2025 (page blocked, not read). Opened an AI hub in Barcelona (2026).
organizations._relationship_reason: Founded by ETH researchers who publish openly on legged-robot RL; a technical talk is realistic, robot access is not (industrial pricing).

organizations.What they build: Founded 2020; builds modular robot arms sold 'robot-as-a-service' (zero upfront) to small and mid-size factories, plus software (RobFlow, RobVision). Raised $100M in Jan 2026 (Lightspeed, Sequoia, Lingotto) and reached a $1B valuation in Oct 2026 via a $40M share sale; CEO moved to the US (Austin assembly). Preparing 'Alfie', a two-armed self-learning robot.
organizations._relationship_reason: Fast-growing startup with a podcast (RobTalk) and showroom; speaker or demo visit is plausible.

organizations.What they build: Barcelona robot maker since 2004 (offices in Toulouse and Bari) building research platforms: TIAGo and TIAGo Pro mobile manipulators (ROS 2, open-source software), the Kangaroo biped and TALOS humanoid, and a new 7-DoF arm with series elastic actuators (<10 kg, 3 kg payload) unveiled at ICRA 2026. Robots in 30+ countries.
organizations._relationship_reason: Sells to universities and runs many EU research projects; has a French office (Toulouse), so a joint project, demo or student discount is realistic.

organizations.What they build: Robotics division of Swedish measurement group Hexagon AB. Builds AEON, a wheeled-leg humanoid (165 cm, 60 kg, 2.4 m/s, 15 kg short-term payload, self-swapping battery, 5 h runtime) for manipulation, inspection and 3D 'reality capture'. Launched June 2025; piloted at BMW Leipzig; Schaeffler committed in April 2026 to deploy at least 1,000 AEONs by 2032.
organizations._relationship_reason: Large group with an industrial focus; a talk is plausible, hardware access unlikely.

organizations.What they build: UK maker of social humanoid robots for museums, events and research: Ameca (61 actuated degrees of freedom, cameras in the eyes, multilingual conversation via its Tritium AI/OS software), desktop versions (Ameca/Ami/Azi Desktop) and custom lookalike robots. Robots can be rented.
organizations._relationship_reason: Rents robots for events; an Ameca at a 42AI event would be a strong visibility move, but rental prices are unknown.

organizations.What they build: Builds the Shadow Dexterous Hand (one of the most advanced five-finger robot hands) and the DEX-EE hand co-developed with Google DeepMind, plus teleoperation setups with tactile sensing. Oct 2026: six-month project with Fraunhofer IFF on dexterous hands for manufacturing. Member of euRobotics.
organizations._relationship_reason: 20+ years working with academic labs; a technical talk or collaboration on teleoperation data is plausible; its hands are expensive (built to order).

organizations.What they build: Motion-plastics manufacturer (~$1B sales) with a low-cost automation unit: ReBeL plastic cobot arm (~8 kg, from $6,899), ReBeL Hand finger gripper (from $2,760), ReBeL Move AMR, and the Iggy Rob humanoid (€47,999). Everything is aimed at being cheap.
organizations._relationship_reason: The cheapest European industrial-grade arm; matches the low-cost hardware hypothesis. igus explicitly targets university R&D, so a discount or sponsored arm is worth asking for.

organizations.What they build: Italian automation company (~50 years old; majority owned by One Equity Partners since late 2024, Stellantis minority): industrial robots, MyCo cobots, MyMR AMRs, MATE exoskeletons and complete production lines; also educational robotics. Oct 2026: Nvidia partnership embedding Isaac Sim and Jetson compute into its robot controllers.
organizations._relationship_reason: Has an educational-robotics offer; worth a sponsorship or demo-material request, terms unknown.

organizations.What they build: Founded 2015 in Gilching (Munich) by Florian Seibel; builds autonomous reconnaissance drones (unmanned aircraft) used heavily in Ukraine. Valuation went from €1B (Series C, May 2025) to $8B with a $1.2B Series D (July 2026).
organizations._relationship_reason: Defense customer base limits what a student lab can do; at most a talk on autonomous drones.

organizations.What they build: UK surgical robotics company making Versius / Versius Plus, a modular, portable keyhole-surgery robot; 45,000+ patients treated (Mar 2026) and US launch in 2026. Oct 2026: Stryker invested ~$400M (preferred equity) with an exclusive option to acquire the company.
organizations._relationship_reason: Medical regulation makes student projects unrealistic; useful only for a talk on surgical robotics.

organizations.What they build: Barcelona startup building reconfigurable 'generalist' factory and logistics robots whose hands, arms and form can be swapped or resized per task (sorting packages, packing clothing...). June 2026: $85M Series A led by CRV (Samsung, Aglaé Ventures in), described as Europe's largest robotics Series A; showroom in central Barcelona.
organizations._relationship_reason: Young, fast-growing and publicly ambitious; open to visibility, but no partnership programme found.

organizations.What they build: Spin-off of the Italian Institute of Technology (IIT) led by Daniele Pucci (iCub/ergoCub/iRonCub lineage). Raised €70M (Dec 2025) to build 'Made in Italy' humanoids; its first humanoid GENE.01 has a touch- and proximity-sensing 'smart skin'.
organizations._relationship_reason: Research-rooted team close to IIT; a talk or research exchange is plausible.

organizations.Organization: Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia (IIT) – iCub Tech
organizations.What they build: Italian research institute that created iCub, an open-source (GPL) child-size humanoid (104 cm) with full-body touch skin; 40+ built for labs worldwide. Also the ergoCub humanoid (Nature Machine Intelligence, July 2026) and the YARP middleware.
organizations._relationship_reason: Open-source designs and an active community; EU research projects and summer schools are a realistic way in.

organizations.What they build: Estonian-founded (2014, HQ and engineering in Estonia, R&D in Helsinki) maker of six-wheeled sidewalk delivery robots: 10M+ autonomous deliveries with ~3,000 robots in 8 countries (2026). In 2026 it left many US campuses to focus on grocery and food retailers.
organizations._relationship_reason: Largest European autonomous-robot fleet; good case study for a talk on fleet autonomy.

summary: Leaders: Germany dominates European robot platforms - NEURA (up to $1.4B Series C), Agile Robots/Franka ($8.5B valuation), RobCo ($1B), KUKA; plus Universal Robots (DK), ABB (CH, sale to SoftBank blocked in China), ANYbotics (CH), PAL (ES), Hexagon AEON (SE).

Money: 2026 brought record rounds for humanoid/generalist platforms (NEURA, Agile, Theker $85M Series A, Generative Bionics EUR70M) and for defense drones (Quantum Systems $8B valuation); surgical (CMR/Stryker) is consolidating.

Demand: factories (BMW, Schaeffler 1,000 AEONs by 2032), energy inspection (ANYmal X for Equinor), last-mile delivery (Starship 10M+ deliveries) and defense; incumbents (UR, KUKA, Comau) are bolting physical-AI and imitation learning onto their arms.

Hypothesis check: European platform makers sell expensive hardware; the only budget-compatible European arm found is igus ReBeL (~$6.9k); FR3/TIAGo Pro/Shadow are research references to reproduce papers on, not to buy. The low-cost wedge (SO-101/LeRobot) is not contradicted, but these firms are not its suppliers.

Best entry points: PAL Robotics (French office in Toulouse, research-friendly), igus (low-cost hardware, targets universities), Franka community/webinars, Engineered Arts Ameca rental for a visibility event, IIT iCub open-source community; talks from NEURA/ANYbotics/RobCo. Partnership terms are all unknown.
